title: SSE continuity handshake and idempotent chunk-stitching for reliable streaming responses
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Implement a robust continuity layer for streaming responses over SSE that minimizes client-visible failures on transient network issues and supports structured outputs (including function/tool calls) without duplicating side effects.

Summary of specification:
- Connection handshake: when a client opens an SSE stream, server returns a short-lived session token (resume_token) in the first event: 'session: <resume_token>|v=2|ttl=60s'. Token encodes the connection slot, last-ack-seq and an HMAC stamp.
- Chunk model: every output delta is sent as a framed SSE event with metadata headers encoded in the event.data preamble: 'frame_id=<uuid>;seq=<n>;type=delta;boundary=(none|func_start|func_end|snapshot)'. The payload after the preamble is a single JSON string containing either a 'delta' or a 'final' structure.
- Idempotency and stitch rules: frames are idempotent if frame_id is stable across retries. On reconnect, client provides last-seen seq and resume_token. Server replays any frames with seq > last_seen. If replay window is not available (server-side ring buffer eviction), server responds with a special 'snapshot' frame to bring the client to a consistent state. Clients must apply frames in seq order and use frame_id to dedupe duplicates.
- Function/tool calling boundaries: function call initiation is encoded as boundary=func_start with a 'call_meta' object; function payload frames may stream arguments or streaming outputs. A boundary=func_end event marks completion and includes 'call_result_id' and 'durable=true' flag indicating side effects persisted. Clients must not re-invoke persisted calls on replay; server guarantees at-most-once semantic for durable calls by including a call_result_id and maintaining server-side durable log for the call_result_id for the resume TTL.
- Heartbeat & liveness: server will emit lightweight 'hb' frames every 15s in quiet streams: event.type=heartbeat;payload="hb:<ts>". Clients track last hb and trigger reconnect if no data/hb for 45s.
- Reconnect/backoff policy: SDKs should implement exponential backoff with jitter (base=200ms, max=5s) and an adaptive probe: after reconnect, the client performs a 'continuity-check' handshake that includes last_seen_seq; server responds with either 'replay' (frames), 'snapshot', or 'migrate' (session moved to another node) and a new resume_token.
- Compatibility shim: provide legacy compatibility mode for older clients (HTTP/1 SSE w/o resume). For legacy clients server will: include a 'final_state' aggregated snapshot as the last event at stream close and provide a separate polling endpoint (/stream/snapshot/:session) for recovery. The SDKs will negotiate 'features=v2' in a header to opt into resume/heartbeat semantics.

Implementation tasks (server):
1) Per-connection ring buffer persisted in memory with optional redis spillover for durable calls. Buffer stores last N frames (configurable by route).
2) Resume token generation + HMAC using service key; TTL enforcement.
3) Durable call result table keyed by call_result_id for at-most-once semantics for persisted tool calls.
4) Metrics: counters for reconnects, replay_size, snapshot_falls_back, duplicate_frames_deduped, heartbeat_misses.
5) Control endpoint /stream/snapshot that can produce a compact snapshot for clients that lost continuity.

Implementation tasks (client/SDK):
1) Expose onResume(token) and onReconnect callbacks; transparent dedupe using frame_id; ordered apply using seq numbers.
2) Surface reconnection progress in Console via websocket/analytics hooks.
3) Implement function-call boundary helpers to avoid accidental double-invocation if server-side durable metadata is missing.
4) Backoff implementation and continuity-check probe.

Tests and validation:
- E2E with network partitions (tcp kill, SYN drops) and simulated dup/delayed frames.
- Property tests for idempotent apply with duplicate frames and out-of-order arrival.
- Chaos test that force-evicts ring buffer entries to ensure snapshot fallback path works and client recovers consistently.
- Integration tests for function call durability: ensure side effects are not duplicated on replay.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th percentile resume latency < 300ms for replayed windows, snapshot fallback path completes < 2s.
- No duplicated durable side effects in tested scenarios.
- SDKs pass compatibility test matrix (old clients, new clients, partial feature negotiation).

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated: streaming-continuity-v2. Canary rollout 5% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor replay_rate, snapshot_rate, customer-error-rate, duplicate-side-effect incidents. If metrics stable, increase to 25% then 100%.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STREAM/SSE+Continuity+v2 (draft)
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892 (WIP)
